Samuel, it's Paulo at Verde Energia. I've just come out of the board meeting and I need to be straight with you. The board is asking why we signed that supply contract without a force majeure provision. When the regulator suspended the licence, we had no way to seek a remedy, and the whole deal fell through. Nobody is blaming you personally, but they want a note by Monday explaining what happened and what we do differently next time. I said you would look into it. Call me when you have read the file.

Samuel, Diane here. I read your note on the Verde matter and I want to give you one piece of advice before Monday. Do not write it as an apology. Write it as an analysis. If the provision had been in the contract, the company would have had a remedy, and that sentence alone tells the board you understand the risk. Then say what you will require in every future contract: a force majeure provision, a clear termination clause, and a cap on liability. Boards do not want regret. They want the next decision.
